A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adaptive ε-PAL research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated definitions and pseudocode.

before.justification: Section 7 and Tables 2–3 report original simulations comparing Adaptive ε-PAL with PESMO, ParEGO, and USeMO, including accuracy, coverage, MSE, and runtime.

after.justification: Section 7 retains the original simulation results and adds experimentally evaluated qNEHVI results in Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: The pessimistic Pareto-set rule changes from weak dominance in v3 Definition 10 to dominance requiring at least one strict coordinate in v4 Definition 8. Equal lower-confidence vectors therefore no longer exclude each other from this set. The remaining algorithmic framework is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same one-dimensional design space [0,1], two independent squared-exponential GP objectives, and Gaussian observation noise. Adding qNEHVI does not introduce another dataset, task, or test scenario.

E2.justification: v4 adds qNEHVI to the comparisons in Tables 2–3 while retaining PESMO, ParEGO, and USeMO. Original ε-PAL remains excluded because completed runs could not be obtained.

E3.justification: The added qNEHVI experiment specifies 100 iterations, sequential batch size q=1, and multi-start L-BFGS-B optimization. v4 also drops v3's ε/10 sampling-gap assurance while retaining 10,000 uniformly sampled reference points. These reporting changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The same tree-depth sensitivity comparison uses hmax values 24, 10, and 9. No new ablation or robustness analysis appears in the appendices. Figure 4 illustrates algorithm operation rather than reporting a new experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten sampled objective functions, five runs per function with different seeds, and means with 99% confidence intervals in Table 2. The qNEHVI column follows the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 add qNEHVI results: combined accuracy/coverage means of 99%, 96%, 95%, and 60% across the four thresholds, MSE of 10×10^-6, and runtime of 40 seconds. Previously reported numerical entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 replaces non-strict termination and sample-complexity thresholds with strict inequalities in Lemma 3, Theorem 1, and related derivations. It revises dominance inequalities and adds a non-repetition argument to Lemma 10's proof. The principal rates, assumptions, and Proposition 1 construction remain; the explicit parameter formulas already appeared in v3's appendix.

C1.justification: The abstract, principal contributions, and conclusion retain adaptive discretization for Pareto active learning, high-probability ε-accurate recovery, and information-type and metric-dimension bounds. New introductory bullets elaborate existing novelty claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: Section 7.3 qualifies Adaptive ε-PAL's comparative advantage to most evaluation thresholds and discusses qNEHVI's competitive accuracy, MSE, and runtime. The existing tree-depth tradeoff and difficulty obtaining terminating original ε-PAL runs remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds BoTorch implementation access information and configuration details for qNEHVI. Section 6 identifies specific Kung et al. algorithms for the previously described efficient dominance computations, refining implementation documentation without establishing a new computational procedure.

R1.justification: v4 adds Daulton et al. (2021) and positions qNEHVI as a method for noisy hypervolume improvement. The existing related-work discussion and Table 1 are substantially retained; introductory additions elaborate the existing distinction from ε-PAL.

P1.justification: v4 adds introductory challenge bullets, algorithm intuition, and phase explanations. Design-space definitions move from Section 3.2 to Appendix A, and pseudocode moves into the main text. Publication notes and acknowledgments are added. These are localized expansions and rearrangements within the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds the six-panel Figure 4, extends Tables 2–3 with qNEHVI columns, and relocates Algorithm 1 from the appendix to the main text. Figures 1–3 retain identical graphics. Publication headers and float placement also change.

improvement.justification: The added qNEHVI comparison in Tables 2–3 makes the accuracy–runtime tradeoff more informative, while the new intuition and Figure 4 improve accessibility. Strict-dominance and termination revisions address specific boundary issues within the retained framework. These limited gains outweigh a small editorial regression: v4 repeats the runtime discussion.
